data.name: Haysam
data.gender_notes: Haysam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root h-y-s meaning 'to live, to be alive'. This name is often given to boys born during the daytime. The name Haysam carries the meaning “Alive, living” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Haysam usually hope their child will grow to embody alive, living and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Haysam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Alive, living.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haysam total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

Historically, the root 'ḥ-s-n' is associated with the concept of ḥusn, meaning goodness or beauty.

historical_references.reference: Haysam ibn Kaladah was a famous poet in the Umayyad period (661-750 AD). He was a native of Kufa in present-day Iraq and is considered one of the foremost poets in the Arabic language. His poetry is characterized by its depth and complexity, and he was known for his mastery of metre, rhyme, and language.
historical_references.context: Famous poet in Iraq, known for his mastery of metre, rhyme, and language.

historical_references.reference: Haysam ibn Matar Al-Qayrawani was a prominent scholar and jurist of the Maliki school of Islamic law in the Fatimid period (909-1171 AD). He was born in Qayrawan in present-day Tunisia. He wrote extensively on various legal issues and is considered one of the leading authorities on Maliki law.
historical_references.context: Prominent scholar and jurist of Maliki school of Islamic law in Tunisia.
